newsitem.title: USA: U.S. corp debt players wrap up deals ahead of Fed.
newsitem.headline: U.S. corp debt players wrap up deals ahead of Fed.

text.p: Activity in the corporate bond primary sector is expected to remain light as players wrap up some pending business before heading to the sidelines ahead of Tuesday's meeting of the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC), dealers said.
"It's very quiet right now...everyone's focused on the Fed," said one syndicate source.
The FOMC, the policy-setting arm of the Federal Reserve Board, will meet tomorrow to vote on monetary policy.
Market players expect policymakers to vote for a 25-basis point tightening in an effort to cool rapid growth.
"There really hasn't been any mention of new names I think people are just getting business squared away," said another syndicate source.
Another factor expected to dampen activity this week is a shortened trading session on Thursday followed by a full close of U.S. financial markets on Friday, dealers said.
U.S. financial markets will be closed in observance of the Good Friday holiday.
PSA The Bond Market Trade Association has also recommended an early close on Thursday, 1400 EST/1900 GMT, for the U.S. credit market, ahead of the holiday.
Despite the threat of higher interest rates, several issuers are still expected to move forward with their planned debt offerings, dealers said.

Among this week's expected deals is WorldCom Inc's $1.5 billion senior note offering which is expected to consist of maturities between seven and 10-years. The offering will be underwritten by Salomon Brothers Inc, the company said.

Proceeds from WorldCom's offering will be used primarily for the repayment of bank debt, general corporate purposes and to fund expansion. The offering will be a partial drawdown from a $3.0 billion shelf registration filed in February.
Millipore Corp is also expected to issue $200 million Baa3/BBB rated two-part debt offering one day this week, sources said.
The deal is expected to consist of $100 million in five-year debt and $100 million 10-year debt. The deal is expected to be underwritten by JP Morgan Securities and CS First Boston, sources said.
Looking ahead, other companies have begun to emerge as debt issuers over the coming weeks, syndicate sources said.
CS First Boston is rumored to be readying a $2.0 billion debt deal for JC Penney in early April, sources said.
Among private placement debt offerings, Ralphs Grocery Co issued $155 million in 11 percent eight-year 144A senior subordinated notes via BT Securities.
Also, on tap is Spanish Broadcasting System's $250 million two-part 144A deal via sole manager CIBC Wood Gundy.

The deal consist of $75 million in senior notes due 2004, price talk is seen at 10.50 percent area. The second tranche for $175 million is for senior exchange preferred securities. Price talk is seen between 13.25-13.50 percent, sources said.
Sterling Chemical is also expected to set $150 million in in 144A senior subordinated notes via CS First Boston.
Affinity Group Holdings is expected to set $120 million in 10-year 144A notes via Citicorp Securities.
Another $215 million in 10-year 144A senior subordinated notes is expected to be brought to market by Del Monte Corp, sources said.
In addition, Echo Bay Mines Ltd is expected to issue $100 million in 30-year capital securities via sole manager Goldman Sachs & Co.
Going forward, the calendar for 144A issues continues to grow with at least another $2.0 billion in new offerings slated for future business, dealers said.
Still, while structuring upcoming deals, players are said to be casting a watchful eye on Tuesday's FOMC results before proceeding with offerings, dealers said.
Last week, at least two high-yield debt offerings were postponed as investors watched prices deteriorate ahead of a possible rise in interest rates, dealers said.
InterCel Inc said last Friday it postponed its planned $300 million debt offering due to deteriorating market conditions.

"I don't have to go out right now in this kind of market climate and expose my shareholders to the kind of pricing that is there now," said Allen Smith, chief executive officer and president of InterCel Inc.
InterCel's roadshow was scheduled to begin on Monday, the company said.

In addition, Qwest Communications International Inc's delayed its planned sale of $450 million deal, which includes a $250 million zero-coupon tranche, to this week's business. The deal is also expected to include $200 million 10-year senior notes.
In the government market, the benchmark U.S. Treasury bond is trading up 9/32 at 96.00 to yield 6.94 percent.
